newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SEESAM DECIDES NOT TO PAY DIVIDENDS.
newsitem.headline: SEESAM DECIDES NOT TO PAY DIVIDENDS.

text.p: The shareholders of Estonian insurance company Seesam on Thursday approved board proposal not to pay dividends from last year's profit of 3.1 million kroons.
Shareholders decided to assign the profit to equity, Toomas Abner, the company's chairman, told Reuters.
Seesam collected premiums of 35.5 million kroons last year and made payments of 13 million kroons.
Its subsidiary, life-insurer Seesam-Elu, had a loss of 200,000 kroons, Abner said.
Seesam-Elu collected premiums of 600,000 kroons and made no payments.
Seesam share capital is ten million kroons, which is owned by Finland's Pohjola Group (44.6 percent), American International Group (29.6 percent), Uhispank (20 percent) and others.
Seesam-Elu's shareholders are Uhispank with 40 percent, Seesam 30 percent and Pohjola with 30 percent. Its share capital is 12.7 million kroons.
